candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.source_attribution: 1 Enoch 5:4, trans. R.H. Charles (1912). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

'But ye — ye have not been steadfast, nor done the commandments of the Lord' — the address to the unrighteous after the natural-theology argument of chs 2-5. The transgression is specifically of the COMMANDMENTS, not of vague moral sensibility: 1 Enoch presupposes the Mosaic covenant as the standard by which the elect are measured. The Tewahedo reading takes this as the canonical Jewish covenant-theology basis that the Christian moral catechesis presupposes; the Sermon on the Mount intensifies but does not abrogate the prior commanded standard.

Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.source_attribution: 1 Enoch 5:7, trans. R.H. Charles (1912). PD. Cf. Mt 5:5 + Ps 37:11.
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

'But to the elect there shall be light and joy and peace, and they shall inherit the earth' — the climactic blessing on the righteous, anticipating the Beatitude 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth' (Mt 5:5 = Ps 37:11). The triple gift (light + joy + peace) Tewahedo eschatology reads as the proper inheritance of the resurrection saints: not merely escape from suffering but positive participation in divine glory. The 'inherit the earth' is read in Tewahedo eschatology as the new-creation earth, restored and glorified, not the present fallen earth.
